proofLevels.name: OBSERVABLE
proofLevels.meaning: The implementation or live behavior can be inspected.

proofLevels.name: ENFORCED
proofLevels.meaning: Executable machinery rejects a prohibited state or operation.

proofLevels.name: TESTED
proofLevels.meaning: Automated qualification or self-tests exercise the mechanism.

proofLevels.name: BENCHMARKED
proofLevels.meaning: Quantitative results exist under a defined protocol.

proofLevels.name: EXTERNALLY_VALIDATED
proofLevels.meaning: Independent creators, evaluators, organizations or market outcomes provide evidence.

claims.label: Browser-native construction
claims.title: The product is built where you use it.
claims.summary: Diamond Gate public products demonstrate repository-owned HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with WebGL/WebGL2 and GLSL where spatial graphics require them.

practical.title: You can inspect the actual product, not just a description of it.
practical.body: The public experience is built directly in the browser. You can open the working surfaces and see the result yourself without needing to understand the underlying graphics stack.
practical.boundary: This does not mean every project will be framework-free, or that native construction automatically guarantees speed, security or low energy use.

engineering.title: Repository-owned browser construction remains directly observable.
engineering.body: Demonstrated surfaces use HTML, CSS and JavaScript owned in the repository, with direct browser graphics technologies used where the experience requires them.
engineering.boundary: This claim is about demonstrated public surfaces, not a universal requirement imposed on every future build.

proof.title: Inspect the demonstrated surfaces.
proof.body: These public routes provide direct observable evidence of the construction approach.
proof.boundary: Observable evidence establishes that the implementation can be inspected. It does not by itself establish benchmark superiority.

claims.label: Page Excellence
claims.title: Required quality conditions were demonstrated as capable of stopping delivery.
claims.summary: The former public Page Excellence implementation demonstrated a fail-closed qualification boundary. Its public executable implementation is retired; successor capability is preserved in the separately governed private repository.

practical.title: The demonstrated qualification model did not treat execution alone as completion.
practical.body: Preserved evidence shows required quality conditions could stop a page operation rather than allowing technical execution to stand in for a finished experience.
practical.boundary: The public implementation is retired. This statement does not authorize or forward private execution and does not claim defect-free software.

engineering.title: Historical public evidence records a fail-closed qualification gate.
engineering.body: Before retirement, the public Page Excellence entry gate could emit a BLOCK disposition when a required condition was non-passing. The executable implementation has been removed from the public execution surface.
engineering.boundary: Current private execution authority must be resolved independently inside the private repository.

proof.title: Inspect the immutable pre-retirement evidence.
proof.body: The public implementation remains inspectable at the immutable P2C execution-base commit; current public main no longer exposes the Page Excellence executable core.
proof.boundary: Private successor preservation is continuity evidence, not public execution authority.

claims.label: Bounded execution
claims.title: Work can be constrained to the exact operation that was admitted.
claims.summary: A preserved public carrier rejected arbitrary command fields, validated admitted identity and scope, and bound delegated execution to exact repository state.

practical.title: One approved task does not have to quietly become a different task.
practical.body: The preserved public mechanism kept execution attached to the exact work that had been admitted rather than allowing an open-ended command surface to decide what happened next.
practical.boundary: This is a historical public demonstration. The retired public carrier is not represented as today’s active public execution mechanism.

engineering.title: The preserved carrier enforced exact-head, descriptor and scope constraints.
engineering.body: It rejected arbitrary command fields, resolved closed executable descriptors, validated admitted identity and scope, and bound delegated execution to exact repository state.
engineering.boundary: The public implementation was intentionally retired. Historical evidence remains valid as evidence of what was demonstrated.

proof.title: Inspect the preserved implementation and its retirement state.
proof.body: The historical implementation remains available at the preserved evidence commit, while the current public path represents retirement state.
proof.boundary: This does not claim that the retired public carrier is currently active.

claims.label: Exact state binding
claims.title: Project identity can be tied to exact repository state.
claims.summary: The preserved public governance implementation bound operation identity, admitted paths, source identities and content digests to exact repository state.

practical.title: A project does not have to rely on memory about what “current” means.
practical.body: The demonstrated approach attached important project facts to exact repository state so a moving branch name or changing session could not silently redefine the operation.
practical.boundary: This is not a blanket cryptographic-security claim and is not represented as a current public runtime.

engineering.title: Operation identity, admitted paths and source identity were explicitly bound.
engineering.body: The preserved implementation attached operation identity, admitted paths, source identities and content digests to exact repository state rather than relying on branch labels or session memory.
engineering.boundary: The evidence supports exact-state enforcement inside the demonstrated repository lifecycle.

proof.title: Inspect the preserved state-binding evidence.
proof.body: The carrier and successor gate provide the preserved public evidence for this claim.
proof.boundary: Not a claim of universal cryptographic security.

claims.label: Blinded governance evaluation
claims.title: The simplified control system was tested under unseen governance conditions.
claims.summary: The milestone consolidation landed at repository PR #1000—the project’s thousandth pull request—followed by PR #1003 lean cleanup. The surviving governance candidate was then operationally reconfirmed, frozen, and evaluated in a 160-case blinded comparison plus a separate 40-case one-shot holdout against a competent guarded baseline.

practical.title: The thousandth pull request became a milestone, but the evidence came afterward.
practical.body: PR #1000 materially simplified the control plane, and PR #1003 removed additional obsolete machinery. The surviving governance system was then exercised again, frozen, and challenged with previously unseen conditions. The authorized conclusion is that it preserved legitimate-operation completion while retaining discrimination against adverse governance conditions within the tested protocol.
practical.boundary: The pull-request number is historical provenance, not technical evidence. This bounded benchmark does not establish universal reliability, enterprise scale, external certification or superiority outside the frozen evaluation design.

engineering.title: Generalization was tested after the PR #1000 consolidation and PR #1003 lean cleanup.
engineering.body: The evaluation came after deliberate control-plane reduction and post-consolidation operational reconfirmation. Candidate freeze remained separate from the hidden cases; the protocol used a 160-case blinded comparative set plus a 40-case one-shot holdout against a competent guarded baseline. The public conclusion is limited to preservation of legitimate completion and adverse-condition discrimination within those tested conditions.
engineering.boundary: Secret seeds, private oracle material and hidden evaluation payloads remain outside the public evidence surface. Neither the milestone PR number nor the benchmark authorizes claims beyond the frozen protocol.

proof.title: Inspect the consolidation provenance, benchmark boundary and disposition.
proof.body: The public summary records PR #1000 as the milestone consolidation, PR #1003 as the lean cleanup, the subsequent operational reconfirmation, frozen evaluation structure, case counts, authorized conclusion and explicit non-claims without exposing private evaluation material.
proof.proofState: Current benchmark evidence · post-PR #1000/#1003 · 160 blinded + 40 one-shot holdout
proof.boundary: The published record intentionally withholds private evaluation material and does not represent the result as external validation or Software TRL 8.

claims.label: Operation succession
claims.title: A continuing project can receive a fresh, bounded successor state.
claims.summary: A preserved successor-packet compiler transformed predecessor operation documents into fresh successor packets while rejecting forbidden scope, authority and stale-head changes.

practical.title: Continuing work can preserve its identity instead of starting from guesswork.
practical.body: The demonstrated mechanism carried forward the parts of an operation that were still valid while refusing undeclared changes to scope, authority or repository state.
practical.boundary: This was a repository-operation successor compiler, not a general-purpose website compiler, and it is not represented as currently active after public retirement.

engineering.title: Successor packets were compiled from constrained predecessor state.
engineering.body: The compiler transformed predecessor operation documents into fresh successor packets, rejected forbidden scope or authority changes, refused undeclared stale-head bindings and emitted a compiler receipt.
engineering.boundary: The public implementation was later replaced by a fail-closed retirement handoff.

proof.title: Inspect the preserved compiler and current retirement path.
proof.body: The preserved compiler and self-test remain inspectable at the historical evidence commit.
proof.boundary: The evidence supports repository-operation succession, not a universal compiler claim.

claims.label: Continuity & recovery
claims.title: Stale authority does not have to be silently treated as current.
claims.summary: Preserved public gates and self-tests demonstrated differential continuity, operation succession, instrument lifecycle and recovery/requalification behavior.

practical.title: When context changes, the system can refuse to pretend nothing changed.
practical.body: The demonstrated continuity machinery checked whether authority and qualification were still valid instead of silently carrying stale state forward as if it were current.
practical.boundary: This does not establish uninterrupted service availability under external infrastructure failures or claim current public execution by the retired implementation.

engineering.title: Continuity and recovery were treated as governed state transitions.
engineering.body: Dedicated gates and self-tests covered differential continuity, operation succession, instrument lifecycle and recovery/requalification, with stale authority or qualification prevented from silently becoming current truth.
engineering.boundary: These public implementations were later retired from the public execution surface.

proof.title: Inspect the preserved continuity gate and self-test.
proof.body: The preserved public repository contains executable evidence for differential continuity.
proof.boundary: Not a claim of uninterrupted service availability.

claims.label: Proof levels
claims.title: Different kinds of proof answer different questions.
claims.summary: Observable, Enforced, Tested, Benchmarked and Externally Validated are intentionally different evidence states.

practical.title: You should be able to tell how strong a claim really is.
practical.body: A live demo is useful, but it is not the same thing as an automated test, a benchmark or independent validation. The labels keep those differences visible so stronger language has to earn stronger evidence.
practical.boundary: A higher proof level does not automatically make a product better; it describes the kind of evidence available for the specific claim.

engineering.title: Proof level and time-state are separate dimensions.
engineering.body: Proof level answers how the mechanism was demonstrated. Time-state answers whether the public implementation is current or historical. A claim can therefore be historically tested without being a current public runtime.
engineering.boundary: The evidence model classifies claims; it does not replace the underlying implementation, test protocol or external validation.

proof.title: The proof ladder is the public classification contract.
proof.body: Every claim should disclose enough information to distinguish inspection, enforcement, automated testing, quantitative benchmarking and independent validation.
proof.boundary: Classification is only useful when underlying evidence remains inspectable and the claim boundary remains explicit.

claims.label: Claim boundaries
claims.title: Precision is part of the product.
claims.summary: Diamond Gate deliberately withholds marketing phrases that require evidence not yet established publicly.

practical.title: You should not have to decode inflated technical language.
practical.body: If the evidence does not support a phrase, the phrase stays out. That keeps the public promise attached to what can actually be demonstrated.
practical.boundary: The absence of these phrases is deliberate. They can be adopted later only when the corresponding evidence exists.

engineering.title: Marketing vocabulary is constrained by evidence state.
engineering.body: Claims such as enterprise scale, industry leadership, universal security or first-of-kind status require distinct benchmark, validation, threat-model or prior-art evidence. They are not inferred from implementation complexity alone.
engineering.boundary: Technical sophistication is not itself evidence for comparative, security, scale or novelty claims.

proof.title: The boundary list is part of the credibility contract.
proof.body: These phrases remain outside authorized public claim language until the relevant evidence is established.
proof.boundary: The page makes claim limits inspectable rather than burying them in fine print.
